title: Ginkgetin reverses cisplatin resistance in cervical cancer by regulating the Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathway to induce ferroptosis.
authors: Wang, Fei; Liu, Yuqin; Wang, Liehong; Bai, Yufang
one_liner_zh: 该研究探讨银杏双黄酮通过Nrf2/HO-1通路诱导铁死亡逆转宫颈癌顺铂耐药，分子对接仅用于小分子-蛋白亲和力分析，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: This study investigates whether Ginkgetin(GK) reverses cisplatin(DDP) resistance in cervical cancer cells by modulating the Nrf2/HO-1 signaling axis to induce ferroptosis, and preliminarily elucidates its underlying mechanisms. DDP-resistant cervical cancer cell line HeLa/DDP was used for in vitro experiments. Cell proliferation was assessed by CCK-8 assay; migration and invasion capabilities were evaluated via wound healing and Transwell assays; colony formation assays measured proliferative capacity. Molecular docking analyzed the binding affinity of GK to Nrf2, HO-1, and GPX4 proteins. Intracellular ROS and Fe(2+) levels were detected using fluorescent probes. Ferroptosis-related indicators including GSH, MDA, SOD, and CAT were measured by biochemical detection. Western blot analyzed expression of key proteins. Mechanistic validation employed the Nrf2 activator sulforaphane (SFN) and ferroptosis inhibitor ferrostatin-1 (Fer-1). An in vivo subcutaneous xenograft mouse model was established to observe the reversal effect of GK on DDP-resistant tumors, combined with histopathological and immunohistochemical analyses of tissue morphology and protein expression. GK significantly inhibited the proliferation of HeLa/DDP cells and enhanced their sensitivity to DDP. Combined treatment of GK and DDP notably suppressed proliferation, migration, invasion, and colony formation abilities of HeLa/DDP cells. Molecular docking revealed strong binding affinity between GK and Nrf2. Combination treatment markedly increased ROS and Fe(2+) levels, reduced antioxidant capacity (GSH, SOD, CAT), induced lipid peroxidation with upregulated ACSL4 expression, and downregulated Nrf2, HO-1, and GPX4 expression. Transmission electron microscopy demonstrated characteristic mitochondrial morphological changes of ferroptosis. In vivo, co-treatment significantly reduced tumor volume of DDP-resistant xenografts, enhanced DDP's antitumor efficacy, improved histopathological structures, and modulated related protein expression. GK induces ferroptosis by inhibiting the Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathway, thereby reversing DDP resistance in cervical cancer cells. These findings provide a potential novel therapeutic strategy for clinical management of cervical cancer.
abstract_zh: 本研究探讨银杏双黄酮（Ginkgetin, GK）是否通过调节Nrf2/HO-1信号轴诱导铁死亡（ferroptosis）来逆转宫颈癌细胞对顺铂（cisplatin, DDP）的耐药性，并初步阐明其潜在机制。采用DDP耐药宫颈癌细胞系HeLa/DDP进行体外实验。通过CCK-8法评估细胞增殖能力；划痕愈合和Transwell实验评估迁移和侵袭能力；克隆形成实验测定增殖能力。分子对接分析GK与Nrf2、HO-1和GPX4蛋白的结合亲和力。使用荧光探针检测细胞内ROS和Fe(2+)水平。通过生化检测测定铁死亡相关指标，包括GSH、MDA、SOD和CAT。Western blot分析关键蛋白表达。机制验证采用Nrf2激活剂莱菔硫烷（sulforaphane, SFN）和铁死亡抑制剂ferrostatin-1（Fer-1）。建立体内皮下异种移植小鼠模型，观察GK对DDP耐药肿瘤的逆转效果，并结合组织病理学和免疫组织化学分析组织形态及蛋白表达。GK显著抑制HeLa/DDP细胞增殖，并增强其对DDP的敏感性。GK与DDP联合处理显著抑制HeLa/DDP细胞的增殖、迁移、侵袭和克隆形成能力。分子对接显示GK与Nrf2之间具有强结合亲和力。联合处理显著增加ROS和Fe(2+)水平，降低抗氧化能力（GSH、SOD、CAT），诱导脂质过氧化并上调ACSL4表达，同时下调Nrf2、HO-1和GPX4表达。透射电子显微镜显示铁死亡特征性线粒体形态变化。体内实验中，联合处理显著减小DDP耐药异种移植瘤体积，增强DDP抗肿瘤疗效，改善组织病理结构，并调节相关蛋白表达。GK通过抑制Nrf2/HO-1信号通路诱导铁死亡，从而逆转宫颈癌细胞对DDP的耐药性。这些发现为宫颈癌的临床治疗提供了潜在的新型治疗策略。
